data.name: US Virgin Islands
data.summary: The USVI applies the US Internal Revenue Code as its own income tax (the 'mirror code'), with 'Virgin Islands' read for 'United States'. A bona fide resident files only with the VI Bureau of Internal Revenue and pays the same rates as on the mainland: 20% on long-term gains and qualified dividends, up to 37% on other income. Whether the 3.8% NIIT is mirrored is unclear. EDC incentives (90% income tax reduction) cover only qualifying business income, not a passive portfolio. No local inheritance or wealth tax was found; US federal estate tax still reaches US citizens (and US-situs assets of non-citizens).

regimes.name: Bona fide residence (mirror code)
regimes.description: Mirror-code income tax paid to the USVI at US federal rates on worldwide income. No local estate/inheritance tax found.
regimes.eligibility: Bona fide residence tests of IRC s. 937 (presence, tax home, closer connection). Non-US citizens need US immigration status to live in the USVI.

capital_gains.summary: Long-term capital gains are taxed at the mirrored US rates, top 20% (plus 25% unrecaptured real-estate depreciation, 28% collectibles). A bona fide VI resident (including a US citizen) satisfies the US filing obligation by filing with the VI (IRC s. 932(c)). The NIIT (3.8%) does not directly apply; the IRS tells residents to ask the VI about mirrored application.

open_questions: Whether the USVI applies a mirrored 3.8% NIIT is not confirmed (IRS Pub. 570); rates exclude it.
For gains on US-source/non-VI assets, IRC s. 934 prevents the VI from granting reductions (e.g. EDC) on non-VI income.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Mirror code: US long-term capital gains rates (top 20%) apply as VI tax. Held over one year assumed.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trader status as under US rules (mark-to-market election possible).

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed under the mirror code: qualified dividends at up to 20%, ordinary dividends at up to 37%. Under the mirror, which foreign (including US mainland) companies' dividends count as 'qualified' is not settled in the sources opened.

dividends.treaty_network: US tax treaties do not apply to the VI as a separate jurisdiction.

inheritance.summary: No USVI inheritance, estate or gift tax was found. US federal estate and gift tax continues to apply to US citizens resident in the USVI unless citizenship was acquired solely by birth or residence in a possession (IRC s. 2209). A non-US citizen domiciled in the USVI is a nonresident alien for federal estate tax and is taxed only on US-situs assets (e.g. shares in US companies) (Form 706-NA).

residency.tax_residency_test: Bona fide residence under IRC s. 937: presence test (e.g. 183 days), no tax home outside the VI, no closer connection elsewhere (IRS Pub. 570).

corporate.summary: Mirror code CIT 21%. Economic Development Commission (EDC) beneficiaries get up to 90% income tax reduction on qualifying business income (requires a qualifying VI business); IRC s. 934 limits benefits on non-VI income.

data.us_citizen_notes: A US citizen who is a bona fide USVI resident for the whole year files with the VI only and has no US income tax liability (IRC s. 932(c)); the VI tax equals the mirrored US tax, so there is no saving on portfolio income. EDC 90% reductions apply only to qualifying VI business income. US estate and gift tax continues to apply (IRC s. 2209 exception only for citizenship acquired via a possession).
open_questions: Qualified dividend status under the mirror code.

succession.name: U.S. Virgin Islands
succession.summary: The U.S. Virgin Islands have no forced heirship for children in the sources found, and Title 15 follows Uniform Probate Code ideas. Common-law trusts apply. No private foundation law was found and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force for the United States.
succession.family_claims: Title 15 of the Virgin Islands Code follows the Uniform Probate Code. Whether it gives a surviving spouse an elective share was not verified.
succession.foreign_law_note: No source read states the Virgin Islands' conflict rule for a foreign national's estate.
succession.trust_note: HCCH shows the United States as signatory only, with no extension. Fiduciary relations sit in Title 15, chs. 51-65. No private foundation statute was found.
open_questions: Elective share and family allowance rules not read.
Title 15 text was seen only as a table of contents.
Trust and foundation statutes not verified.
Private foundations: no source found either way; not finding a foundation law is not evidence that there is none.
